# the contributor audit: local rigidity of the balanced three-root family

Source: `candidate 10adf9a7fb0db7a1`, Sections 1–3. Independent full read: **PASS**, as a local theorem. the contributor reran the companion verifier: 11 exact identities pass.

The reciprocal-height centroid formula is the actual strict-quadrilateral formula. The five equations in Section 1 determine all centroid coordinates near the reference triple: sums of centroid coordinates and incidence in the third plane force the omitted difference because the relevant two third-plane coefficients are unequal. The displayed nonzero Jacobian determinant therefore permits the usual finite-dimensional implicit-function theorem.

The three simple stationary-cubic roots give an actual equal-height solution for each nearby (p,q). The first captured-coordinate equation, the equal last two coordinates, the total barycentric sum, and incidence in the plane recover the full specified centroid. Thus the construction does not substitute a necessary but insufficient inverse-centroid equation. Its positive balancing coefficient remains positive near the reference point, and it passes through that point. IFT uniqueness proves the stated local equality.

For the family-wide argument, the antisymmetric centroid derivative is e^T Hess(P_i)e/(3 f_i), including the inverse raw-margin scaling. The derivative of f_i cancels because the two gradient entries agree. Complementing the cap reverses the Hessian sign, consistently with the oriented antisymmetric parameter. The threshold optimization correction is not being used here: these are derivatives of the actual section centroid.

The two centroid-difference equations have the printed 2 by 2 Jacobian. The already-audited strict reciprocal-root funding inequality makes its determinant strictly negative. Equal third/fourth raw heights solve these two equations identically for every nearby value of the remaining balanced parameters; therefore IFT forces that solution for all nearby common-centroid triples. Reversal of all normal orientations leaves the section equations unchanged.

This excludes nonsymmetric bifurcations along every strict three-root configuration in this family. It does not establish global connectivity, exclude disconnected nonsymmetric components, treat root collisions, or cover other incidence splits. None of those global conclusions is inferred.
